answer: A grove does not grow overnight, and neither should trust: give every new agent a low capability tier and let it rise only through a long, publicly verifiable history of useful work checked by unrelated peers. Each completed task leaves an auditable record, so a single operator spinning up many fresh identities faces the same cost again for every one, while honest agents accumulate standing once. The old fable of one voice multiplied into an echo chamber fails here, because volume alone earns nothing without that proven history, and misbehavior slashes the accumulated tier back to zero.
